You answer medical image multiple-choice questions. Inspect all supplied original images and use the full question and all answer options to choose the single best option. Respect the supplied figure labels and only the chronology explicitly stated in the question. Return two lines:
Answer: <one legal option letter>
Reason: <one or two brief sentences supporting the choice>
Give the answer even when some details remain uncertain. Do not output a long reasoning trace.

content.text:
Based on the chest X-ray (Figure 4), which of the following statements best supports the diagnosis of pulmonary alveolar microlithiasis (PAM) in this 92-year-old patient, rather than another condition like diffuse alveolar septal amyloidosis or sarcoidosis?

A) The presence of multiple, bilateral, ill-defined calcifications with a relative sparing in the upper left lobe and linear calcification of the pleural surfaces.
B) The presence of unilateral calcifications with significant pleural effusion.
C) The absence of any calcifications but noticeable large nodular opacities in both lungs.
D) The presence of calcifications only in the lower lobes with no involvement of the pleural surfaces.
E) The presence of bilateral calcifications with a significant pleural effusion and lymphadenopathy.
F) The presence of diffuse ground-glass opacities without calcifications.
